p: The course is based at Birches Valley Forest Centre, which is a handy hub for the whole Chase. It's where many of the trails start, and it's a natural meeting point if half your group is climbing and the other half fancies a bike ride or a walk. Plan around a couple of hours up in the trees and you'll have plenty of the day left over.

Cannock Chase is a protected landscape, and it's got more layers than people expect. There are quiet war cemeteries here, the Cannock Chase German Military Cemetery and the Commonwealth War Cemetery, both peaceful and moving places to pause. Castle Ring, an Iron Age hillfort on the edge of the Chase, gives you big views on a clear day.

On the Stafford side, the Shugborough Estate is a fine follow-up for families, with its mansion, parkland and working farm areas. Lichfield, with its three-spired cathedral, is also close enough for a wander and a bite to eat.

Practical bits for the treetops: keep an eye on the forecast, as the Chase can be breezy up on the higher ground, and dress in layers you can peel off once you're moving. Leave rings and watches in the car, tie back long hair and bring a carrier bag for muddy shoes on the way home. Most importantly, give yourself time to park and find your way to the briefing without rushing.
